title: Flat ambient neighbourhood of an H1-regular flat quotient
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with $B$ finitely presented over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Let $r\geq0$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in B$, put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, and assume $H_1(K_B(f_1,\ldots,f_r))=0$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Assume $B/I$ is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then for every prime ideal $Q\subset B$ containing $I$, there exists $h\in B\setminus Q$ such that $B[1/h]$ is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The ambient algebra $B$ need not be flat over $A$ in advance; neither ring is assumed Noetherian. Empty sequences and zero rings are allowed.

source.place: Tag 063V (lemma-flat-relative-H1-regular), conclusion (1), affine principal-neighbourhood form; its proof by absolute Noetherian approximation, followed by openness of flatness.

proof.text: Choose a presentation $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ and polynomial lifts $F_i$ of the $f_i$. By [lemma-nagata-ring-finite-type-subalgebras], the finite set of coefficients of all $g_j,F_i$ lies in a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra $A_0\subseteq A$. Set $B_0=A_0[x]/(g)$, $f_{i,0}=F_i\bmod(g)$ and $C_0=B_0/(f_{1,0},\ldots,f_{r,0})$. These are finitely presented algebras, the latter with presentation $A_0[x]/(g,F)$. Polynomial scalar extension and the quotient tensor formula give $B_0\otimes_{A_0}A\cong B$ and $C_0\otimes_{A_0}A\cong B/I$, carrying the marked elements to $f_i$. These identifications hold after replacing $A$ by any intermediate subalgebra $A_j$.

source.place: Tag 063V (lemma-flat-relative-H1-regular), finite polynomial presentation and finite coefficient subalgebra paragraph.

proof.text: Index the intermediate finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras $A_j\subseteq A$ containing $A_0$ by inclusion. This is a small nonempty directed set (a subset of the set of subrings of $A$); its colimit is $A$ by [lemma-nagata-ring-finite-type-subalgebras], since every finite coefficient set can be adjoined. Put $B_j=A_j[x]/(g)$ and $C_j=A_j[x]/(g,F)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map] with its algebras $B_0^{\mathrm{there}}=A_0$ and $C_0^{\mathrm{there}}=C_0$. The limiting map is $A\to B/I$, flat by hypothesis; its initial map is finitely presented by step 1. After enlarging $A_0$, $C_0$ is $A_0$-flat and every later $C_j$ is $A_j$-flat. The rings $A_j$ and $B_j$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]: $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian because each nonzero ideal is generated by its least positive integer, and the zero ideal is principal too.

source.place: Tag 063V, application of algebra.tex Tag 02JO (lemma-flat-finite-presentation-limit-flat), followed by Noetherianity of the coefficient models.

proof.text: In the low-degree Koszul complex over this $B_0$, let $Z_0=\ker(d_1:B_0^r\to B_0)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], choose finitely many generators $z_1,\ldots,z_N$ of $Z_0$. Their classes generate $H_1(K_{B_0}(f_0))$, since every homology class is represented by a cycle. For each $j\geq0$, [lem-sfb-koszul-h1-flat-quotient-base-change-surjective] applies to $A_0\to B_0$, $A_0\to A_j$, because $B_0/(f_0)=C_0$ is $A_0$-flat. Thus $H_1(K_{B_0}(f_0))\otimes_{A_0}A_j\twoheadrightarrow H_1(K_{B_j}(f_j))$. Its pure-tensor formula shows that the images of the same $N$ cycle classes generate the target as a $B_j$-module: the source is generated by $[z_a]\otimes1$ over $B_0\otimes_{A_0}A_j=B_j$.

source.place: Tag 063V, finite generation of the first Koszul homology and application of more-algebra.tex Tag 063Q (lemma-base-change-H1-regular).

proof.text: Each image $z_a\in B^r$ is a boundary because $H_1(K_B(f))=0$. Choose $w_a\in K_2(B,f)$ with $d_2w_a=z_a$. Write its finitely many wedge-basis coefficients as polynomial classes in $A[x]/(g)$, and choose polynomial representatives for the coordinates of $z_a$ in $B_0^r$. For every coordinate of $d_2w_a-z_a$, its polynomial representative belongs to $(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ in $A[x]$; choose an expression $\sum_j v_jg_j$ witnessing this membership. Adjoin to $A_0$ every coefficient of these finitely many representatives and witnesses. The resulting finite type subalgebra $A_1\subseteq A$ already has $d_2w_{a,1}=z_{a,1}$ in $B_1^r$: the polynomial identities remain identities over the subring $A_1$. Consequently every generator from step 3 vanishes at stage 1. Its surjection implies $H_1(K_{B_1}(f_1))=0$. This explicitly realizes the source's filtered-colimit killing of finitely many classes without using homology commutation as an unstated lemma.

source.place: Tag 063V, passage to a finite stage killing all first-homology generators; explicit finite-coordinate version of its colimit argument.

proof.text: Let $Q_1$ be the inverse image of $Q$ under $B_1\to B$. It is prime, contains $I_1=(f_{1,1},\ldots,f_{r,1})$, and $T=(B_1)_{Q_1}$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and the definition of localization at a prime. The localized Koszul complex is $K_T(f_1/1)$ by [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso]. Exact localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] preserves $\ker d_1=\operatorname{im}d_2$, so its first homology is zero. Apply [lem-per-h1-koszul-quasi-regular] to this ring $T$: the polynomial-to-associated-graded map for the images of $f_1$ is an isomorphism. All these elements belong to the maximal ideal of $T$, so [lem-pur-quasi-regular-noetherian-local] shows that they form a regular sequence in $T$.

source.place: Tag 063V, Noetherian case using Tag 063T; regularity supplied by more-algebra.tex Tag 062I and algebra.tex Tag 061S.

proof.text: The $A_1$-flat module $C_1$ remains $A_1$-flat on localization at $Q_1/I_1$ by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness]. The quotient-localization isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] identifies that algebra with $T/I_1T$. For $0\leq j\leq r$ set $T_j=T/(f_{1,1}/1,\ldots,f_{j,1}/1)$. Every $T_j$ is a nonzero Noetherian local ring: its ideal lies in the maximal ideal, its quotient is local, and Noetherianity follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] applied to a quotient. Starting with the established $A_1$-flatness of $T_r$, descend on $j$. The image of $f_{j,1}/1$ in $T_{j-1}$ is in its maximal ideal and is a nonzerodivisor by step 5, and its quotient is $T_j$. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-local-nonzerodivisor-flat-lift] to conclude $T_{j-1}$ is $A_1$-flat. Thus $T=T_0$ is $A_1$-flat. For $r=0$ this is just the initial flatness of $T_r$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-openness-of-flatness] to $A_1\to B_1$ and its rank-one free module $M=B_1$. The ring map is finitely presented by its presentation in step 1, and $M$ is finitely presented over $B_1$. Step 6 puts $Q_1$ in its open flat locus. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], choose $h_1\notin Q_1$ with $D(h_1)$ contained in that locus. Then $(B_1)_{h_1}$ is $A_1$-flat: for each prime of this ring, the corresponding prime $P\in D(h_1)$ has stalk $(B_1)_P$, flat over $A_1$ by the choice of locus. Localizing the base at its contraction preserves this flatness by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization]; the stalk identity follows from the fraction universal property. The local criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-map-local-criterion] for $A_1\to(B_1)_{h_1}$ now gives the assertion.

source.place: Tag 063V, final Noetherian flat-locus paragraph, using algebra.tex Tag 00RC (theorem-openness-flatness).

proof.text: Let $h\in B$ be the image of $h_1$. Since $Q_1$ is the inverse image of $Q$, $h\notin Q$. Base change of the $A_1$-flat module $(B_1)_{h_1}$ gives an $A$-flat module by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]. The canonical algebra identification [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-localization-away-base-change], followed by $B_1\otimes_{A_1}A\cong B$, identifies it with $B[1/h]$ (tensor factors may be interchanged by $a\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes a$). This proves the claimed principal neighbourhood. If $B$ is the zero ring, or $I=B$, no prime $Q\supseteq I$ exists and the conclusion is vacuous. If $r=0$, the quotient hypothesis already says $B$ is $A$-flat and $h=1$ works; the construction above also includes the empty cycle and equation families.

source.place: Tag 063V, base-change reduction from the Noetherian model; principal-open refinement and degenerate cases made explicit.

proof_origin.place: Tag 063V (lemma-flat-relative-H1-regular), proof of (1); the filtered-colimit paragraph is expanded by polynomial witnesses for finitely many boundaries; Tag 063T and its Tag 062U induction give the Noetherian case.
